description: A general meeting: what mattered, what was discussed, what is still open.
context: A general meeting between the participants. Write for someone who was not there and has to act on it: what was decided, what is open, what happens next. Prefer concrete facts, numbers, names and dates over general statements, and never invent anything that was not said.

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.instructions: Three to five bullets with the outcomes that matter most: decisions, commitments, changes of direction, deadlines. The lead is a short noun phrase naming the topic; the text says what was concluded, not what was discussed.

sections.heading: Full Summary
sections.instructions: One bullet per topic in the order it came up. The lead names the topic; the text gives the substance in one to three sentences and names who argued for or asked for what where that matters. Skip small talk and logistics.

sections.heading: Open Questions
sections.instructions: Questions raised but not answered, and points explicitly deferred, one bullet each. The lead names the question in a few words; the text says who raised it and what depends on it. Omit the section when there are none.
